standard_prerequisites.name: Nakayama's lemma
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, the lemma allowing the surjectivity of a map of modules to be checked modulo a nilpotent ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the surjectivity of the ring map from the Artinian local ring to the local ring of the preimage from the equality of residue fields.

core_obligations: Reduce to affine pieces (proof lines 2067-2074): the target decomposes as a disjoint union of spectra of Artinian local rings finite over the field, and the source of a monomorphism towards such a disjoint union is a scheme, so one considers the preimages X_i of the pieces, each of which has at most one point.

Analyse a one-point preimage (proof lines 2074-2082): if X_i has a point then it is the spectrum of a zero dimensional local ring B_i and the ring map from A_i to B_i is an epimorphism, so the two residue fields agree; since the maximal ideal of A_i is nilpotent, Nakayama's lemma shows that the map is surjective, hence B_i is a finite local algebra over the field.
Conclude (proof lines 2082-2084): each piece is a finite local algebra over the field, so by the structure result the map to the spectrum of the field is locally quasi-finite.
proof_roadmap: Decompose the target into Artinian pieces finite over the field and reduce to the preimages of the pieces.
Show each nonempty preimage has a single point with a zero dimensional local ring mapping onto it as an epimorphism, then use Nakayama to get finiteness.
Apply the structure result to conclude local quasi-finiteness.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a monomorphism of algebraic spaces over a field whose target is locally quasi-finite over the field has locally quasi-finite source (statement lines 2061-2065). The proof (proof lines 2067-2086) decomposes the target into Artinian pieces finite over the field, reduces to the preimages of those pieces, and uses an epimorphism of zero dimensional local rings together with Nakayama's lemma to conclude that those preimages are finite local algebras over the field. H2: a two-step reduction with three inputs, written out in full.
